newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Hagemeyer to buy rest of joint venture.
newsitem.headline: Hagemeyer to buy rest of joint venture.

text.p: Trading company Hagemeyer NV said on Wednesday it will buy the remaining 50 percent of its Hong Kong-based joint venture Hagemeyer Cosa Liebermann (HCL) from Switzerland's Anova.
"In exchange for its interest in HCL, Anova will be issued 3,380,000 new ordinary Hagemeyer shares," the Dutch group said in a statement.
In addition to the payment in new Hagemeyer shares, which represents a 7.5 percent stake in the company, a cash payment of 70 million guilders ($41 million) will be made.
This values the transaction at more than 500 million guilders.
Hagemeyer said the deal will be concluded before the end of this year and added the capital increase would not affect its earlier forecasts of 1996 earnings per share.
"The full impact of this strategic move will materialise as from 1997 and it will have a positive effect on Hagemeyer's future earnings per share," the company said.
Hagemeyer said Anova has the intention of being a long-term investor in the company and the Swiss group will have a representative in Hagemeyer's supervisory board.
HCL was set up in 1994 as a 50-50 joint venture combining the activities of Hagemeyer and Anova's Cosa Liebermann in the Asia-Pacific Region.

The venture has annual sales of about 1.3 billion guilders so that the intended transaction will boost Hagemeyer's turnover by about 650 million guilders. Last year the Dutch group, in which Hong Kong's First Pacific Co has a controlling stake, posted a turnover of 5.72 billion guilders. ($ = 1.706 Dutch Guilders)
